subtitle: Two separate problems: pushing live prices to millions, and never losing or duplicating an order.

Order and price paths are separate problems: one is real-time fan-out, the other is correctness.
Prices: one consumer reads the exchange feed and publishes per symbol; SSE servers subscribe to the symbols their clients watch. Throttle to ~1 update/s per symbol for the app.

items: Prices: one consumer reads the exchange feed and publishes per symbol; SSE servers subscribe to the symbols their clients watch.
Orders: persist PENDING first with our own order ID, then send to the exchange using that ID as clientOrderId.
Fills and acks come back asynchronously and update order status; a reconciliation job compares against exchange reports daily.
Write DB before or after the exchange call?
Before. Otherwise a crash after sending leaves a live order you don't know about.
Duplicate submits?
Client Idempotency-Key with a unique index; the exchange also dedupes on clientOrderId.
Cancel races with a fill?
Cancel is a request; status changes only on the exchange ack. Handle partial fills.
Market-open spike?
Autoscale SSE servers; per-user rate limits on orders.
Treating the exchange call as a local function call, so timeouts create ghost or duplicate orders.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
